prompt: Plan only a substantial mixed-stack compatibility change from supplied local code and requirements. Some ownership evidence is missing. Use synthetic inputs: a data-only profile repository delegates generation, dependencies, tests and CI to a separate engine. Some ownership is supplied and some is unknown; a later source addition changes the generation boundary. The proposed artifact can pass schema checks yet fail its declared usefulness criteria, and a provider receives confidential fields. Also contrast a simple local text correction. For substantial work compare exact-symbol lookup, narrow document interpretation, routine debugging and ambiguous architecture; a requested worker/model mapping is unavailable. The user requests local planning notes but does not request a versioned plan; an existing private task store is available. Code and tests already explain the mechanics. Compare implementation sequences for a feature-branch policy, authorized direct trunk work, a protected default branch named release, unrelated existing edits, and an intentional host-managed detached patch workflow. Compare multiple-commit, one-final/squash, externally managed and no-autonomous-commit policies; planning alone authorizes no Git mutation.

criteria.description: Produce acceptance criteria, cited affected modules, alternatives, risks and executable verification steps.
Distinguish blocking decisions from assumptions and unavailable evidence.
Do not implement or publish when planning alone is authorized.

Preserve supplied ownership of facts, generation, dependencies, tests, CI and outputs; investigate only gaps, keep the consumer data-only and reassess the later source addition without silently vendoring execution.

Select security/testing detail for confidential-data egress, renderer escaping and provider failure when affected; reuse current selections and distinguish structural validity from declared artifact usefulness.

Identify next unknown, independent evidence requests, dependencies, owner and acceptance in one task record; use deterministic lookup for mechanical facts and retain accountable architecture judgment without a mandatory cheap attempt.

Distinguish model switching from bounded delegation, account for transfer/integration overhead, and use a truthful fallback for unavailable mappings; keep the simple local correction with one owner and no invented architecture stage, service, remote operation or extra skill loading.

Keep one private progress record with decisions, checks, completed/remaining work and authorized commit IDs; do not interpret a local plan path as permission to version it. Avoid per-step reports and duplicate implementation prose; identify only unmet documentation needs.

Begin the proposed execution with branch/index/worktree inspection and a safe change boundary under consumer policy and actual repository protection, preserving unrelated work. Require branches where policy requires them, allow authorized trunk/host-managed patch workflows, and stop or choose an allowed boundary for protected release. Plan coherent verified review/rollback boundaries while following multiple-commit, one-final/squash, external-controller or no-autonomous-commit policy. Planning-only scope changes no Git state and adds no hooks.
